Rating seems to be flawed calculations.. I had high hopes for this app on helping me make good choices for my family after seeing it when reading about the “dirty dozen” list. In neither case can I trust the rating this app provides.

Misleading information. I downloaded this app to review products that are commonly promoted as being nontoxic or eco-friendly. In my opinion this app has a very misleading ranking system. There are four general categories on which an item is ranked (skin sensitivities, developmental/hormone disrupting, asthma causing, and environmentally conscious) based on these factors the product(s) ingredients are ranked on a scale A-F. For example, let’s take a laundry detergent for instance with 10 ingredients 8 of those ingredients are ranked A, 1 is ranked B, and the last ranked C. A average person would assume that the rating would perhaps be B, but the overall raking will be listed as C which for most people would automatically deem as “toxic or not safe.” Then they have their “EWG healthy living” approved products that have met strict standards… but let’s take another laundry detergent for instance that has 22 listed ingredients, 13 of the ingredients are ranked C, 5 are ranked B, and 4 are ranked A. Now of course the general rating for this product is not posted, but you could only assume it would not be higher than a C, but is given a “stamp of approval.” EWG claims that they break down each product by hazard and data availability, but the rankings to me don’t make much sense when the “bad” is outweighing the “good.” This app like a lot of other “health” apps need some work or need to have more information listed as to how and why the products are getting these specific rankings. As a consumer I would still do your own research and come to your own conclusions about what you believe is safe.

I just bought a lip balm from Honest because it had the EWG stamp of approval but as soon as I got it out of the box, I saw that the product is contained in a tub of #1 plastic, which is known to leech chemicals. Instead of relying on this app, one should do the research on products, ingredients, and packaging on their own.

I don’t understand the rating system. I believe the developers really need to consider other factors that should be used when rating items, ESPECIALLY animal treatment/welfare. I didn’t see any information about animal testing or ingredients in the make up section. When it comes to animal proteins, I am seeing proteins that are pastures and grass fed get LOWER ratings than animal proteins from factory farms (like Fosters).

For example: Peanut butter, Natures Promise organic crunchy, EWS score of 1-when you look at the nutritional label, it does not have saturated fat recorded, which is 2.5%.
